details:
There is an AWFUL refresh loop happening in the Avatar Descriptor if inspecting your Avatar in Play Mode, specifically with Face Tracking section expanded with many mapping rows exposed (all ~102).

**My Findings:**

- `FaceTrackingEditorContext.Tick` increments every `EditorApplication.update;`, the `ParameterBehavior` and `BlendshapesSet` drawers treat a new Tick as invalidation, so their per-element state and validation refresh on every editor frame.

- `FaceTrackingBlendshapesSetDrawer` draws ALL ~102 mapping rows insaide a 280px scroll view with no visibility culling.

- Every `EditorApplication.hierarchyChanged` bumps `HierarchyRevision`, causing `CollectAmbiguousMeshPaths` to run `GetComponentsInChildren<Transform>(true)` and `CalculateTransformPath` on EVERY transform of the Avatar on the next repaint.

- Cost scales with the number of Parameter Behaviors (in my testing, I had 38). Tools that add Parameter Behaviors in Play Mode like VRCFury or NDMF make this behavior much worse.

This is a severe performance vulnerability that should be patched as soon as possible.
title: [3.10.6] Inspecting an avatar root in Play Mode with the Avatar Descriptor's Face Tracking foldout open causes severe Editor lag
